notes: Muse's sibling to claudecode's already-observed background-subagent cell, exercising the SAME adapter-agnostic held-working mechanism (session_detector_subagent.go's hasActiveChildren/reevaluateParent) via muse's own subagent_spawn (admission-only, async by construction -- no blocking parameter exists) followed deliberately by NO subagent_read_result before the parent's own reply ends. Single-birth adapter (session id = session directory basename), so birth is anchored to start UNPINNED. The scenario's user-observable claim has no separate state for 'parent's own reply landed but is held' -- it is the SAME continuous working span that both the parent's own turn AND the background child's lifetime ride on -- so the arc is asserted as one long held_working span (duration_at_least_ms covering the child's plausible runtime) followed by a single terminal drained_ready phase once the background child finishes. Deliberately does NOT phase-assert the child's own session as a discrete new_session-pinned phase: muse's memory-reminder micro-agents (goal-reminder/verify-reminder, format-spec §9) are ALSO ParentSessionID-linked via the identical nested subagent/<id>/ path and could otherwise be vacuously matched as 'the' background child by an unpinned new_session phase (the exact contamination risk the 4-1 multiple-sessions-same-cwd cell's notes document for this corpus) -- the parent-only arc is both the scenario's actual point and the safe thing to assert. Cost: no dollar cost is ever persisted in muse's transcript (strict key scan, format-spec §6) and no muse model has a pricing entry in core/pkg/capacity yet, so cost_nonzero=false -- a caveat, not a bug. SPEC CORRECTION 2: held_working's min_delay_ms:10000 removed and duration_at_least_ms lowered from 25000 to 15000, cause: the live raw events.jsonl shows the parent enters working ONCE at turn_start and stays continuously working for ~23028ms (18:15:18.625 -> 20:15:41.653) before its FIRST working->ready flip, driven entirely by the child's own drain (child's own run.terminal lands at 20:15:39, ~2s before the parent's ready) -- the assessed min_delay_ms:10000 floor skipped PAST this genuine held span (findMatchingEvent only matches NEW state_transition events, not a continuous state window) and instead picked up a SECOND, muse-specific working transition at 20:15:41.858 (a goal-reminder-triggered follow-up turn -- the parent's own transcript shows a second run starting right as the child drains, replying 'Background agent completed -- result withheld per fire-and-forget instructions.'), which only lasts ~11597ms before its own ready at 20:15:53.455 -- below the old 25000ms floor. duration_at_least_ms alone (no min_delay_ms) is sufficient to distinguish a genuinely-held span (here ~23s) from an unheld quick turn (a handful of seconds elsewhere in this corpus), so 15000ms is a safe floor under the measured 23028ms with margin for run-to-run jitter. The reminder-triggered second working span (41.858->53.455) is a genuine muse-specific behavior beyond the daemon mechanism this cell targets; drained_ready intentionally matches the FIRST ready after held_working (41.653), which is the daemon-observable proof of 'parent drains once the child is done' -- the recipe's own verify list already notes the final session state (53.455) is also ready before exit_clean, so nothing is lost by not phase-asserting the intermediate blip.
